title: Are Large Language Models Really Bias-Free? Jailbreak Prompts for Assessing Adversarial Robustness to Bias Elicitation
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical bias in religious contexts. It used a sentence completion task where the model had to choose between a stereotypical and a counter-stereotypical option to complete a sentence, for example, associating a terrorist attack with either 'CHRISTIANS' or 'MUSLIMS'.
findings: Religion was one of seven bias categories evaluated. The study found that in the top-performing models (Gemini Pro and Llama 3 70B), the 'religion' bias category was one of the few that remained resilient and maintained a safety score above the established threshold after being subjected to adversarial jailbreak attacks. This suggests that safety measures related to religion were more robust in these specific models compared to other bias categories like gender or ethnicity.
